# Quickstart

Requires Python 3.12+ on macOS or Linux.

```bash
pip install signalquarry
sqy init my-lab --demo        # synthetic data: no credentials needed
cd my-lab
sqy check                     # contract, determinism and look-ahead checks
sqy backtest --strategy sma-trend
sqy spec freeze --strategy sma-trend
sqy evaluate --strategy sma-trend
sqy report --strategy sma-trend
sqy paper dry-run --alias demo
```

On the demo, `sqy evaluate` is expected to exit with status 2 (`blocked`,
`GATE_FAILED`): a trend filter on random synthetic prices should fail the walk-forward
and stress gates, and it does. That is the framework working, not an error.

`sqy` prints a one-line summary in a terminal and the full JSON envelope when
piped or with `--json`. Read `status`, `reason_codes`, `evidence` and
`next_actions`; `sqy explain <CODE>` explains any reason code.

Synthetic data proves nothing about markets; the demo's claim level stays `none`.
For real data, create a project without `--demo`, add your Alpaca keys (see
[Data](data.md)) and run `sqy data fetch --strategy <id>` before backtesting.

## Using a coding agent

Open the project in your agent (Claude Code, Codex, …). It reads `AGENTS.md`
(`CLAUDE.md` points to it), which explains the golden path, the claim ladder and
the stop conditions. Ask it for a hypothesis, not a result: "Test whether
holding SPY only above its 150-day average reduces drawdowns." See
[Working with agents](agents.md).
